decision: Establish a canonical, additive design-token and UI-primitive layer without changing the current production cascade.
invariants: Do not link the new stylesheets into production templates until route/template adoption and visual QA are complete.
Do not replace or rename existing theme attributes or legacy selectors in this foundation PR.
Keep all new component selectors namespaced with the in- prefix.
Preserve WCAG 2.2 AA contrast targets, visible keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, and RTL compatibility.
Do not change application runtime behavior, routes, D1 schema, Worker configuration, secrets, or production data.
Register the token and primitive stylesheets after existing application styles; keep all component classes opt-in and namespaced.
Do not change the existing global Light/Dark preference behavior or the reader's independent theme preference in this foundation PR.
Do not claim visual QA or page-family migration from static CSS contract tests.
Worker HTML response assembly must include both design-system assets for every mapped HTML template, not only the root index shell.
acceptance: The design-system contract test passes in the Cloudflare source-validation workflow.
Architecture ownership governance recognizes this same-PR feature contract.
Runtime adoption is handled by a separate reviewed integration change with desktop, mobile, and RTL visual QA.
Every theme supplies a complete semantic role set and automated WCAG AA text contrast checks pass.
Component usage guidance distinguishes CSS styling from application-owned keyboard behavior, focus management, persistence, authorization and async state.
Application shell loads both new stylesheets without bulk-migrating legacy templates.
All Worker-served HTML templates receive the design-system token and primitive stylesheets exactly once through the shared releaseStyles list.
The design-system documentation contains the 33 explicit Worker route mappings, dynamic route patterns, renderer families and page-family migration acceptance gates.
releaseBoundary: Foundation only; not production-adopted and not a deployment authorization.
